title: Inverse images along immersions preserve pro-etale limits
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $u:Y\to X$ be a locally closed immersion, meaning a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $u^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] preserves all small limits of sheaves of sets and of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For every sheaf of commutative rings $R$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the inverse-image functor $\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(u^{-1}R)$, with module sheaves as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], is additive, exact, and preserves all small limits. Its underlying abelian sheaf is $u^{-1}$ of the underlying abelian sheaf, and its scalar action is $u^{-1}$ of the original action under the finite-product comparison. More generally, if $S$ is a ring sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $c:u^{-1}R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ is a ring-sheaf isomorphism, then the functor $M\mapsto u^{-1}M\otimes_{u^{-1}R,c}S$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is exact and preserves all small limits, including countable products. Smallness is relative to the fixed sheaf universe. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed. The isomorphism hypothesis on $c$ is essential to this last assertion; no assertion is made for extension of scalars along a general ring map.

proof.text: For a closed immersion of affine schemes, the extra adjunction $i^{\mathrm{Sh}}_!\dashv i^{-1}$ is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-inverse-image-left-adjoint]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits] with $R=i^{-1}$. This proves preservation of every small limit cone in the affine closed case. Limits exist by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise].

For an open immersion $j:W\to X$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the slice site over $W$. Under this identification inverse image is restriction, $F|_W(V\to W)=F(V\to X)$: in the inverse-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] the object $V$ regarded over $X$, with its diagonal map to $W\times_XV$, is terminal in the indexing diagram, and restriction is already a sheaf. Since limits of sheaves of sets are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], evaluation of either side of the limit comparison at $V\to W$ is the same limit of sets. Thus open inverse image preserves all small limits.

proof.text: Let $i:Z\to X$ be an arbitrary closed immersion. Cover $X$ by affine opens $X_a$. By the affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion], $Z_a=i^{-1}(X_a)$ is affine and $i_a:Z_a\to X_a$ is a closed immersion. Write $j_a:X_a\to X$ and $k_a:Z_a\to Z$ for the opens. The equality $i k_a=j_a i_a$ and [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] give $k_a^{-1}i^{-1}\cong i_a^{-1}j_a^{-1}$. Restrict the canonical limit comparison to $Z_a$. Step 2 moves restriction past the limit on its target, and steps 1 and 2 identify its source with the same limit; the maps are those induced by the original cone projections, so the restricted comparison is invertible. These restrictions detect isomorphisms: for any site object $V\to Z$, the opens $V\times_ZZ_a$ cover $V$, and compatible local inverses glue uniquely by the sheaf condition. Hence the comparison is invertible globally.

proof.text: Factor the locally closed immersion as $Y\xrightarrow{i}W\xrightarrow{j}X$ using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Inverse-image composition [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] identifies $u^{-1}$ with $i^{-1}j^{-1}$. Applying step 2 then step 3 to any small limit cone proves the set-valued assertion.

For abelian sheaves, [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-underlying] identifies underlying sets of abelian inverse image with set inverse image. A small limit of abelian sheaves is the sectionwise set limit equipped with componentwise addition, zero and negation: these operations satisfy the group identities on each projection, the sheaf condition follows from [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-sheaf-iff-underlying-sets], and coordinatewise factorization proves the universal property. Consequently the set limit comparison from step 4 is a homomorphism and an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. Exactness and additivity of abelian inverse image follow from [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact].

For an $R$-module $M$, apply the finite-product-preserving set inverse image to its addition, ring operations and scalar action $R\times M\to M$. Every module law is an equality of composites of these maps, so functoriality preserves each law; naturality makes the action compatible with restriction. This gives an $u^{-1}R$-module with underlying abelian sheaf as in step 5, and applies equally to module homomorphisms. Kernels and cokernels have the underlying abelian kernels and cokernels, respectively: their inherited action or quotient action is defined componentwise, with sheafification for the cokernel, as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus step 5 gives exactness and additivity on modules. Limits are created on underlying abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]. The comparison from step 5 is linear since all its projections are linear; its inverse is linear because a bijective linear map has a linear inverse. Hence module inverse image preserves all small limits.

If $c:u^{-1}R\to S$ is an isomorphism, identify $S$ with $u^{-1}R$ through $c$. The balancing map $u^{-1}M\otimes_{u^{-1}R,c}S\to u^{-1}M$ sends $m\otimes s$ to $c^{-1}(s)m$; its inverse is $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. The balancing relation in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] proves both composites are identities, and the maps are natural in $M$. Changing the ring through an isomorphism preserves kernels, cokernels and all limits by the same componentwise descriptions of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]. The asserted exactness and limit preservation therefore follow from step 6; a countable product is the limit of the discrete diagram indexed by the positive integers.
